title: Tray pricing: Is it worth it?
summary: Tray.io pricing can be complicated and hard to understand. Here's what you need to know about how tasks, agents, and hidden costs work before you choose a plan.
body_markdown:
As a software engineer who's built hundreds of integrations over the years, I demand a lot from[integration platforms](https://zapier.com/blog/best-enterprise-integration-platforms/) . In the case of Tray, the promise is that you can orchestrate workflows and enterprise-grade AI agents. That's a claim many other platforms make, but Tray has been in the automation business for more than a decade, so there's some level of credibility there.


But no matter how great a platform is, price matters. Tray doesn't publish rates for its plans, but it does list a starting price and explain how it charges. So I dug into what Tray.ai actually costs. This breakdown covers the plan tiers, what each one includes, and how Tray's pricing compares to Zapier.

## What is Tray?


Image source:[Tray](https://tray.ai/demo)


Launched in 2012, Tray is a low-code iPaaS built for enterprise-level organizations. Teams can use it to automate complex, multi-system processes like syncing CRM records, routing leads, managing IT service requests, and moving data between apps without writing custom code. Users can build what they need via a visual workflow builder, with access to 700+ pre-built connectors.


Tray rebranded from Tray.io to Tray.ai in 2024, reflecting a noticeable pivot to AI. The core[workflow platform](https://zapier.com/blog/workflow-automation-software/) remains the foundation, but Tray has since built an agent development layer that helps teams build, govern, and deploy[AI agents](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-agent/) .


## Tray pricing overview


To get an exact number for Tray, you'll need to contact its sales team, as plan pricing is quote-based. Tray does say its pricing starts at $50 a month and is based on usage, measured in tasks (and, for its Helix product, Helix Compute Units), with no per-user, per-connection, or per-runtime fees.


In practice, costs depend on three factors: the package you choose, your usage volume, and optional add-ons (which, of course, means extra money). Tray typically quotes a fixed annual cost based on an annual volume commitment, with usage above your plan settled at a true-up. Each trigger firing, connector step, and loop or boolean pass counts as a task.


Here's what to expect from the three base plans and the add-ons. (There's also a 30-day free trial with 1 million tasks, and no card or sales call is required.) Note that support is business-hours on every plan, with a paid upgrade (Tray Advantage Plus) for 24/7 support and enhanced SLAs.


### Pro package


The Pro package includes the platform's core features, such as automation and integration tools, the connector library, and Tray Build, Tray's low-code, AI-assisted workflow builder.


At the Pro level, you get three "workspaces" (separate environments for creating, organizing, and securing your workflows), along with seven days of insights and log retention. Tray positions Pro for teams with a specific use case, so it's a good fit if you're starting with one focused project.


### Team package


The Team package provides the same core functionality as Pro, but bumps up the available workspaces to 20. You also get 30-day insights, expandable log retention (seven days to start), log retention management, and Guardian Log Masking, plus access to optional add-ons, including HIPAA compliance features, SSO, regional hosting, and extended log retention.


This level is good for organizations covering multiple use cases within a department, so it's a natural next step once a single project has outgrown Pro.


### Enterprise package


The Enterprise package pulls out all the stops, offering all of the features from Pro and Team, plus unlimited workspaces. It also adds security and compliance features like single sign-on and log streaming to enable real-time monitoring.


This plan is aimed at organizations that span multiple departments or partner integrations, including those with strict data residency requirements. The governance and security add-ons available at lower tiers are included by default.


Tray also offers a Tray Embedded solution for SaaS companies that want to build integrations directly into their own products.


### Agent Gateway for MCP


Agent Gateway for MCP is Tray's governed control layer for[MCP (Model Context Protocol)](https://zapier.com/blog/mcp/) . MCP gives AI agents a standardized way to connect to external tools and data, rather than hitting raw APIs directly. Agent Gateway ties each call to a named user, logs it in one audit record, and works with MCP clients like Claude, Cursor, and VS Code. It's sold as part of Tray's Agent Development add-on, and access is enabled at the organization level through your Tray team.


The notable feature is composite tools, which let you bundle multi-step workflows into a single MCP tool. When teams prompt an AI agent, it can make one governed call, rather than many separate calls across your apps. Tray says this can cut token costs by up to 10x, though it doesn't publish a methodology for that figure.


### Merlin Agent Builder


Merlin Agent Builder is Tray's no-code AI agent builder, with guardrails, audit logs, and human-in-the-loop approval built in. Agents can use your Tray workflows as tools, and Tray says every major LLM is pluggable, so you can switch models without rebuilding your agents.


You can build custom agents with Merlin Agent Builder or start from its ITSM and HR accelerators. For example, Tray's demos show an ITSM agent that handles software provisioning and access issues and logs tickets, and an HR service desk agent that checks entitlements and applies rules.


Merlin Agent Builder is part of Tray's Agent Development add-on, which is priced separately through sales, so it's an extra cost on top of your base plan. Since Tray bills on usage, expect agent activity to count toward your tasks, as each trigger firing, connector step, and loop or boolean pass counts as one.


## Who is Tray best for?


Traditionally, Tray has been a popular choice for IT teams in mid- to large-sized enterprises. It has been geared toward programmers and other technical users who need to develop complex, multi-system workflows but either can't afford MuleSoft or don't need such a robust API ecosystem.


With the transition to Tray.ai and the introduction of Merlin Agent Builder and Agent Gateway, though, Tray is moving toward a broader audience. Natural-language workflows and agent building open the door to non-technical teams, making Tray a feasible option for smaller tech shops and business units outside of IT.


Even so, Tray is a complex environment that gets expensive fast, especially when there are solid[Tray alternatives](http://tray.io/) . Zapier, for example, can handle many of the same use cases at a cheaper, more transparent price point, and it offers more than 9,000


native integrations, compared to 700+ for Tray.


## Tray vs. Zapier pricing


[Tray and Zapier](https://zapier.com/blog/tray-vs-zapier/) serve many of the same use cases, but they take very different approaches to pricing. Tray requires a sales conversation to get a quote for its plans, though it does list a starting price of $50 a month and offers a 30-day free trial with no card or sales call required. That means you can try it first, but you'll still need to talk to sales to know what a production plan costs.


[Zapier's pricing](https://zapier.com/pricing) is transparent and based on the number of tasks used. Each action in a workflow counts as a single task—and you're not charged for triggers, filters, formatting, branching, or other built-in logic. There's a free plan for small operations, and the paid plans start at $19.99/month. You can even get up to 25 users on Zapier for only $69/month (total, not per user), and only once you're ready to scale do you talk to Sales about an enterprise plan.


And because Zapier connects to 9,000+


apps (well over 10 times Tray's 700+ pre-built connectors), you're getting more bang for your buck. Combined with[enterprise-grade security features](https://zapier.com/security-compliance) , you can build safely from wherever you work.
